chapter_title: Concerning the Four Works of the Ambassador

fills.notes: The doors of the firmaments open in the advance of the descending/ascending Power and close after it, marking ordered passage through discrete heavens. The pair “open … and shut behind him” constrains the missing adverbial complement to the symmetric “before him.”

The clause compares two lights: the purified/released light exceeds “the light that he shall …”. In the oldest substrate this is a contrast between essential light and the derivative light apprehended in manifestation; “see” fits the correspondential idea of lower, perceived light versus higher, intrinsic light.
Accepted as fitting the substrate register: the light-ship is not ‘built’ but ‘manifested’/made visible through the perfection (completion) of the human vessels.

The sentence requires a verb of elevation/setting-forth: he has (i.e., caused to be borne) the living soul, which then “shone forth … over the worlds of enmity.” “Raised up in” keeps the impersonal cosmological mechanics: the soul is elevated into the light-vessel, then its radiance extends over the hostile worlds.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the parallelism of cosmological ‘doors’ (open before / shut behind) and by standard substrate mechanics (purified light contrasted with perceived light; light-ship as manifestation). The final lacuna allows several near-synonyms (set/placed/raised/brought) for the causation of the living soul’s elevation; the chosen fill matches the required ascent-and-radiance sequence but remains tentative.
